 Northwest Notes: Hansen, Mara, Lyles, Nuggets
 By Arthur Hill |
 at November 9, 2026 10:59 am 
 The Trail Blazers didn’t face much adversity during the early part of the season, but that changed over the weekend with back-to back losses to the Lakers and Spurs, writes Sean Highkin of The Rose Garden Report  (subscriber link). Portland looked overmatched against a pair of MVP favorites, as Luka Doncic poured in 53 points on Friday and Victor Wembanyama followed that with 29 points in 24 minutes on Saturday while dominating the game on defense.
 “The start of the third quarter, we were awful,” coach Micah Nori said after Saturday’s game. “We got one or two stops, and then it was … the turnovers again, and just we looked kind of out of sorts. First time all year. If you want to find excuse, you can find excuse. But it’s a big-boy league. They’re on a back-to-back, we’re on a back-to-back. These are going to happen. We’re going to have guys out. I don’t care who’s out. We’ve got to make sure we compete and be who we are. And tonight, I thought was the first time that we kind of got away from that.” 
 One bright spot on Saturday was the play of Yang Hansen , who moved into the backup center role with Robert Williams resting. Yang had 12 points and 10 rebounds for the first double-double of his career, and Highkin observes that he appears to have separated himself from Branden Carlson and Micah Potter in the frontcourt rotation.
 “We just need him to continue to get better,” Nori said. “And I think the more that he continues to play, and he starts to play well, and get sped up, and his communication gets better, that’s only a positive for us. So the more minutes that he can gain, the better that we will reap the benefits of for moving forward. We think highly of him. He’s going to be able to help us.” 
 There’re more from the Northwest Division:
 Thunder rookie Aday Mara credits college coach Dusty May , now with the Mavericks, for helping him develop into an NBA player after his transfer to Michigan, relays Justin Martinez of The Oklahoman (subscription required). “I was overthinking,” Mara said. “I was thinking about how I needed to do everything perfect so I could get the confidence of the coach and how I couldn’t make a mistake and things like that. It was that UCLA mentality that I had. But (May) came and just told me, ‘Don’t worry.’ He just gave me confidence.” 
 When the Timberwolves were short on power forwards this summer, president of basketball operations Tim Connelly reached out to Trey Lyles , who had been playing in Spain, per Jon Krawczynski of The Athletic (free link). Connelly developed trust in Lyles during their time together in Denver, and he has become a valuable reserve after the team was able to add Jonathan Kuminga . “I don’t want to say it’s easy, but I think (it’s) just my adaptability,” Lyles said. “Being able to adapt to different situations has always helped me in my career. So I think this just goes to show another situation where I’m able to do that.” 
 All five Nuggets starters, along with DeMar DeRozan , have been listed as questionable for Monday’s game in Houston due to travel problems following Saturday’s contest in Mexico City, according to Bennett Durando of The Denver Post . Altitude TV reporter Katy Winge explains the team’s lengthy flight delay ( Twitter link ).
